MIN(ps.binding_count) AS binding_count_range, VAR_POP(ps.binding_count) AS binding_count_variance, STDDEV_POP(ps.binding_count) AS binding_count_stddev FROM ports AS p JOIN (SELECT p2.id AS port_id, COUNT(*) AS binding_count FROM ports AS p2 JOIN portsecuritybindings AS b ON p2.id = b.port_id GROUP BY p2.id) AS ps ON p.id = ps.port_id GROUP BY p.status ORDER BY binding_count_range DESC NULLS LAST), SecurityGroupPortStatusCounts AS (SELECT p.STATUS AS port_status, COUNT(DISTINCT p.ID) AS ports_in_security_group FROM SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS AS sgpb JOIN PORTS AS p ON sgpb.PORT_ID = p.ID WHERE sgpb.SECURITY_GROUP_ID = '0008e629-5619-41e0-b86c-4eecfeaacb6c' GROUP BY p.STATUS) SELECT pd.port_id, pd.port_status, pd.ip_address, pd.window_column, pss.binding_count_range, pss.binding_count_variance, pss.binding_count_stddev, sgc.ports_in_security_group FROM PortDetailsForSecurityGroup AS pd JOIN PortSecurityBindingStatsByStatus AS pss ON pd.port_status = pss.status JOIN SecurityGroupPortStatusCounts AS sgc ON pd.port_status = sgc.port_status ORDER BY pd.port_status NULLS FIRST, pd.window_column NULLS FIRST, pd.port_id NULLS FIRST), StatusBenchmark AS (SELECT AVG(ports_in_security_group) AS avg_ports_per_status FROM (SELECT port_status, MAX(ports_in_security_group) AS ports_in_security_group FROM inner_cte GROUP BY port_status) AS s) SELECT i.port_id, i.port_status, i.ip_address, i.window_column, i.binding_count_range, i.binding_count_variance, i.binding_count_stddev, i.ports_in_security_group, sb.avg_ports_per_status AS benchmark, CASE WHEN i.ports_in_security_group > sb.avg_ports_per_status * 1.5 THEN 'HIGH_STATUS' WHEN i.ports_in_security_group < sb.avg_ports_per_status * 0.5 THEN 'LOW_STATUS' ELSE 'AVERAGE_STATUS' END AS status_category FROM inner_cte AS i CROSS JOIN StatusBenchmark AS sb ORDER BY i.port_status NULLS FIRST, i.window_column NULLS FIRST, i.port_id NULLS FIRST

question: For active networks with admin_state_up = 1 that have at least one DOWN port, return the tenant ID, network ID, network name, admin_state_up flag, MTU, the network’s standard attribute updated_at timestamp, and the count of DOWN ports—only for those networks whose DOWN-port count is greater than the average DOWN-port count among all active admin_state_up = 1 networks. Do not return any rounded answers.
generated_sql: WITH active_network_down_counts AS (     SELECT         n.tenant_id,         n.id AS network_id,         n.name,         n.admin_state_up,         n.mtu,         MAX(sa.updated_at) AS updated_at,         COUNT(p.id) FILTER (WHERE p.status = 'DOWN') AS down_port_count     FROM networks AS n     JOIN standardattributes AS sa         ON n.standard_attr_id = sa.id     LEFT JOIN ports AS p         ON p.network_id = n.id     WHERE n.status = 'ACTIVE'       AND n.admin_state_up = 1     GROUP BY n.id ) SELECT     tenant_id,     network_id,     name,     admin_state_up,     mtu,     updated_at,     down_port_count FROM active_network_down_counts WHERE down_port_count > 0   AND down_port_count > (       SELECT AVG(down_port_count)       FROM active_network_down_counts   )
official_measure: BEAVER: the same set of rows
gold_sql: WITH inner_cte AS (WITH DownPorts AS (SELECT p.ID AS port_id, p.TENANT_ID AS tenant_id, p.NAME AS port_name, p.NETWORK_ID AS network_id, p.MAC_ADDRESS AS mac_address, p.DEVICE_OWNER AS device_owner, ia.IP_ADDRESS AS ip_address, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY p.NETWORK_ID ORDER BY p.ID NULLS FIRST) AS window_column FROM PORTS AS p JOIN IPALLOCATIONS AS ia ON p.ID = ia.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN'), ActiveNetworks AS (SELECT n.ID AS network_id, n.NAME AS network_name, n.TENANT_ID AS tenant_id, n.ADMIN_STATE_UP AS admin_state_up, n.MTU AS mtu, sa.UPDATED_AT AS standard_attr_updated_at, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY n.TENANT_ID ORDER BY n.NAME NULLS FIRST) AS window_column FROM NETWORKS AS n JOIN STANDARDATTRIBUTES AS sa ON sa.ID = n.STANDARD_ATTR_ID WHERE n.STATUS = 'ACTIVE') SELECT an.tenant_id, an.network_id, an.network_name, an.admin_state_up, an.mtu, an.standard_attr_updated_at, COUNT(DISTINCT dp.port_id) AS down_port_count FROM ActiveNetworks AS an LEFT JOIN DownPorts AS dp ON dp.network_id = an.network_id AND dp.tenant_id = an.tenant_id WHERE an.admin_state_up = 1 GROUP BY an.tenant_id, an.network_id, an.network_name, an.admin_state_up, an.mtu, an.standard_attr_updated_at HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT dp.port_id) > 0 ORDER BY down_port_count DESC NULLS LAST, an.network_name NULLS FIRST), DownPortAverages AS (SELECT AVG(down_port_count) AS avg_down_ports FROM inner_cte) SELECT i.tenant_id, i.network_id, i.network_name, i.admin_state_up, i.mtu, i.standard_attr_updated_at, i.down_port_count FROM inner_cte AS i WHERE i.down_port_count > (SELECT avg_down_ports FROM DownPortAverages) ORDER BY i.down_port_count DESC NULLS LAST, i.network_name NULLS FIRST

question: For each tenant that has ports on host "drive-59", show the tenant ID, the number of distinct ports on that host, the number of those ports that are administratively up and have port security enabled (matched by MAC address), the secured-port ratio (secured ports divided by total drive-59 ports) rounded to 2 decimals, and the deviation of that tenant’s secured-port ratio from the average secured-port ratio across all such tenants.
generated_sql: WITH host_ports AS (     SELECT DISTINCT         p.tenant_id,         p.id,         CASE             WHEN p.admin_state_up = 1              AND EXISTS (                  SELECT 1                  FROM portsecuritybindings ps                  WHERE ps.port_id = p.id                    AND ps.port_security_enabled = 1              )              AND EXISTS (                  SELECT 1                  FROM allowedaddresspairs aap                  WHERE aap.port_id = p.id                    AND aap.mac_address = p.mac_address              )             THEN 1             ELSE 0         END AS secured_up     FROM ports AS p     JOIN portbindingports AS pb       ON pb.port_id = p.id     WHERE pb.host = 'drive-59' ), tenant_ratios AS (     SELECT         tenant_id,         COUNT(*) AS total_ports,         SUM(secured_up) AS secured_ports,         SUM(secured_up)::numeric / COUNT(*) AS secured_ratio     FROM host_ports     GROUP BY tenant_id ) SELECT     tenant_id,     total_ports,     secured_ports,     ROUND(secured_ratio, 2) AS secured_port_ratio,     secured_ratio - AVG(secured_ratio) OVER () AS deviation_from_avg_ratio FROM tenant_ratios ORDER BY tenant_id

gold_sql: WITH inner_cte AS (WITH HostDrive59Ports AS (SELECT b.PORT_ID, p.TENANT_ID, p.MAC_ADDRESS, SUM(p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) OVER (PARTITION BY b.VIF_TYPE ORDER BY p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID NULLS FIRST) AS window_column FROM ML2_PORT_BINDINGS AS b JOIN PORTS AS p ON b.PORT_ID = p.ID JOIN PORTSECURITYBINDINGS AS psb ON p.ID = psb.PORT_ID WHERE b.HOST = 'drive-59'), AdminUpPorts AS (SELECT p.NAME AS port_name, p.MAC_ADDRESS AS mac_address, psb.PORT_SECURITY_ENABLED AS port_security_enabled, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY p.MAC_ADDRESS NULLS FIRST ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND 1 FOLLOWING) AS window_column FROM PORTS AS p JOIN PORTSECURITYBINDINGS AS psb ON p.ID = psb.PORT_ID WHERE p.ADMIN_STATE_UP = 1), Drive59AdminUpSummary AS (SELECT h.TENANT_ID, COUNT(DISTINCT h.PORT_ID) AS drive59_port_count, COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN a.port_security_enabled = 1 THEN h.PORT_ID END) AS drive59_secured_port_count, ROUND(CAST(CAST(COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN a.port_security_enabled = 1 THEN h.PORT_ID END) * 1.0 AS DOUBLE PRECISION) / NULLIF(NULLIF(COUNT(DISTINCT h.PORT_ID), 0), 0) AS DECIMAL), 2) AS secured_port_ratio FROM HostDrive59Ports AS h JOIN AdminUpPorts AS a ON a.mac_address = h.MAC_ADDRESS GROUP BY h.TENANT_ID) SELECT s.TENANT_ID, s.drive59_port_count, s.drive59_secured_port_count, s.secured_port_ratio FROM Drive59AdminUpSummary AS s ORDER BY s.secured_port_ratio DESC NULLS LAST, s.drive59_port_count DESC NULLS LAST), avg_cte AS (SELECT AVG(secured_port_ratio) AS avg_secured_port_ratio FROM inner_cte) SELECT i.TENANT_ID, i.drive59_port_count, i.drive59_secured_port_count, i.secured_port_ratio, (i.secured_port_ratio - a.avg_secured_port_ratio) AS deviation_from_avg_secured_port_ratio FROM inner_cte AS i CROSS JOIN avg_cte AS a ORDER BY deviation_from_avg_secured_port_ratio DESC NULLS LAST, i.secured_port_ratio DESC NULLS LAST, i.drive59_port_count DESC NULLS LAST

question: For each IPv4 subnet stats row (either DNS nameserver ORDER stats or per-next-hop route-count stats), list the subnet name, network ID, the stats fields, the “reason” label, and the deviation of that row’s range value from the average range among rows with the same reason. Do not return any rounded answers.

gold_sql: WITH inner_cte AS (WITH DnsOrderStats AS (SELECT s.name AS subnet_name, MAX(d."order") - MIN(d."order") AS order_range, VAR_POP(d."order") AS order_variance FROM SUBNETS AS s JOIN DNSNAMESERVERS AS d ON s.id = d.subnet_id WHERE s.ip_version = 4 GROUP BY s.name ORDER BY order_range DESC NULLS LAST), RouteCountStats AS (SELECT s.NAME AS subnet_name, MAX(route_count) - MIN(route_count) AS route_count_range, VAR_POP(route_count) AS route_count_variance, STDDEV_POP(route_count) AS route_count_stddev FROM SUBNETS AS s JOIN (SELECT sr.SUBNET_ID, COUNT(*) AS route_count FROM SUBNETROUTES AS sr GROUP BY sr.SUBNET_ID, sr.NEXTHOP) AS route_stats ON s.ID = route_stats.SUBNET_ID WHERE s.IP_VERSION = 4 GROUP BY s.NAME ORDER BY route_count_range DESC NULLS LAST), CombinedSubnetStats AS (SELECT subnet_name, order_range, order_variance, NULL AS route_count_range, NULL AS route_count_variance, NULL AS route_count_stddev, 'DNS Nameserver Order Stats' AS reason FROM DnsOrderStats UNION ALL SELECT subnet_name, NULL AS order_range, NULL AS order_variance, route_count_range, route_count_variance, route_count_stddev, 'Route Count Stats' AS reason FROM RouteCountStats) SELECT * FROM CombinedSubnetStats ORDER BY subnet_name NULLS FIRST, reason NULLS FIRST), Enriched AS (SELECT i.subnet_name, s.network_id, i.order_range, i.order_variance, i.route_count_range, i.route_count_variance, i.route_count_stddev, i.reason, CASE WHEN i.reason = 'DNS Nameserver Order Stats' THEN i.order_range ELSE i.route_count_range END AS range_value FROM inner_cte AS i JOIN subnets AS s ON s.name = i.subnet_name AND s.ip_version = 4), AvgByReason AS (SELECT reason, AVG(range_value) AS avg_range_value FROM Enriched GROUP BY reason) SELECT e.subnet_name, e.network_id, e.order_range, e.order_variance, e.route_count_range, e.route_count_variance, e.route_count_stddev, e.reason, (e.range_value - a.avg_range_value) AS deviation_from_avg_range_within_reason FROM Enriched AS e JOIN AvgByReason AS a ON e.reason = a.reason ORDER BY e.subnet_name NULLS FIRST, e.reason NULLS FIRST

 )         ELSE h.max_vif_sample_variance     END AS max_vif_sample_variance FROM rolled_up_counts AS r LEFT JOIN host_max_variances AS h   ON h.host IS NOT DISTINCT FROM r.host ORDER BY question: For IPv4 subnets that belong to networks with an RBAC action of 'access_as_shared', return only those subnets whose max-to-running-sum ratio (maximum subnet standard attribute ID over the current row and next 2 rows, divided by the running sum of subnet standard attribute IDs within the IP version group, rounded to 2 decimals) is greater than the average of that same ratio across all such subnets; list the subnet’s name and CIDR along with its tenant ID, network ID, gateway IP, DHCP enabled flag, allocation pool first/last IP, the RBAC target tenant, the running sum, the max-over-next-2 value, and the ratio.
generated_sql: WITH eligible_subnets AS (     SELECT         s.id,         s.name,         s.cidr,         s.tenant_id,         s.network_id,         s.gateway_ip,         s.enable_dhcp,         s.ip_version,         s.standard_attr_id     FROM subnets AS s     JOIN networks AS n         ON n.id = s.network_id     WHERE s.ip_version = 4       AND EXISTS (           SELECT 1           FROM networkrbacs AS nr           WHERE nr.object_id = n.id             AND nr.action = 'access_as_shared'       ) ), subnet_windows AS (     SELECT         es.*,         SUM(es.standard_attr_id) OVER (             PARTITION BY es.ip_version             ORDER BY es.standard_attr_id, es.id             ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW         ) AS running_sum,         MAX(es.standard_attr_id) OVER (             PARTITION BY es.ip_version             ORDER BY es.standard_attr_id, es.id             ROWS BETWEEN CURRENT ROW AND 2 FOLLOWING         ) AS max_over_next_2     FROM eligible_subnets AS es ), subnet_ratios AS (     SELECT         sw.*,         ROUND(             sw.max_over_next_2::numeric / NULLIF(sw.running_sum, 0),             2         ) AS ratio     FROM subnet_windows AS sw ), subnet_scores AS (     SELECT         sr.*,         AVG(sr.ratio) OVER () AS average_ratio     FROM subnet_ratios AS sr ) SELECT     ss.name,     ss.cidr,     ss.tenant_id,     ss.network_id,     ss.gateway_ip,     ss.enable_dhcp,     ap.first_ip,     ap.last_ip,     nr.target_tenant,     ss.running_sum,     ss.max_over_next_2,     ss.ratio FROM subnet_scores AS ss JOIN networkrbacs AS nr     ON nr.object_id = ss.network_id    AND nr.action = 'access_as_shared' LEFT JOIN ipallocationpools AS ap     ON ap.subnet_id = ss.id WHERE ss.ratio > ss.average_ratio

generated_sql: WITH ports_with_both_bindings AS (     SELECT p.id, p.status, p.standard_attr_id     FROM ports AS p     WHERE EXISTS (         SELECT 1         FROM securitygroupportbindings AS sgpb         WHERE sgpb.port_id = p.id     )       AND EXISTS (         SELECT 1         FROM portsecuritybindings AS psb         WHERE psb.port_id = p.id     ) ), standard_attr_cv AS (     SELECT         status,         STDDEV(standard_attr_id) / NULLIF(AVG(standard_attr_id), 0) AS standard_attr_id_cv     FROM ports_with_both_bindings     GROUP BY status ), ip_address_length_cv AS (     SELECT         p.status,         STDDEV(LENGTH(ia.ip_address))             / NULLIF(AVG(LENGTH(ia.ip_address)), 0) AS ip_address_length_cv     FROM ports AS p     JOIN ipallocations AS ia       ON ia.port_id = p.id     WHERE EXISTS (         SELECT 1         FROM portsecuritybindings AS psb         WHERE psb.port_id = p.id           AND psb.port_security_enabled = 1     )     GROUP BY p.status ), status_ip_coverage AS (     SELECT p.status     FROM ports AS p     GROUP BY p.status     HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT p.id) FILTER (         WHERE EXISTS (             SELECT 1             FROM ipallocations AS ia             WHERE ia.port_id = p.id         )     ) > 0.75 * COUNT(DISTINCT p.id) ) SELECT     s.status,     s.standard_attr_id_cv,     i.ip_address_length_cv FROM standard_attr_cv AS s JOIN ip_address_length_cv AS i   ON i.status IS NOT DISTINCT FROM s.status JOIN status_ip_coverage AS c   ON c.status IS NOT DISTINCT FROM s.status

question: For each network whose number of ports that are both in status 'DOWN' and have port security enabled is greater than the average such count across all networks, list the network ID, that down-and-secure port count (and the overall total of down-and-secure ports), and also the maximum (within that network) of the range, variance, and standard deviation (using STDDEV only and never STDDEV_POP) of allowed address-pair counts per port (considering only ports that have at least one allowed address pair). Do not return any rounded answers.
generated_sql: WITH per_network_down_secure_counts AS (     SELECT         n.id AS network_id,         COUNT(DISTINCT p.id) FILTER (             WHERE p.status = 'DOWN'               AND ps.port_security_enabled = 1         ) AS down_secure_port_count     FROM networks AS n     LEFT JOIN ports AS p         ON p.network_id = n.id     LEFT JOIN portsecuritybindings AS ps         ON ps.port_id = p.id     GROUP BY n.id ), overall_counts AS (     SELECT         AVG(down_secure_port_count) AS average_count,         SUM(down_secure_port_count) AS overall_total     FROM per_network_down_secure_counts ), per_port_address_pair_counts AS (     SELECT         p.network_id,         p.id AS port_id,         COUNT(*) AS address_pair_count     FROM ports AS p     JOIN allowedaddresspairs AS a         ON a.port_id = p.id     GROUP BY p.id ), per_network_address_pair_stats AS (     SELECT         network_id,         MAX(address_pair_count) AS max_address_pair_count,         MAX(address_pair_count) - MIN(address_pair_count) AS address_pair_count_range,         VARIANCE(address_pair_count) AS address_pair_count_variance,         STDDEV(address_pair_count) AS address_pair_count_stddev     FROM per_port_address_pair_counts     GROUP BY network_id ) SELECT     c.network_id,     c.down_secure_port_count,     o.overall_total AS overall_down_secure_port_count,     s.max_address_pair_count,     s.address_pair_count_range,     s.address_pair_count_variance,     s.address_pair_count_stddev FROM per_network_down_secure_counts AS c CROSS JOIN overall_counts AS o LEFT JOIN per_network_address_pair_stats AS s     ON s.network_id = c.network_id WHERE c.down_secure_port_count > o.average_count ORDER BY c.network_id

MIN(port_pair_count) AS pair_count_range, VAR_POP(port_pair_count) AS pair_count_variance, STDDEV_POP(port_pair_count) AS pair_count_stddev FROM SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS AS sgpb JOIN (SELECT p.ID AS port_id, COUNT(*) AS port_pair_count FROM PORTS AS p JOIN ALLOWEDADDRESSPAIRS AS aap ON p.ID = aap.PORT_ID GROUP BY p.ID) AS port_stats ON sgpb.PORT_ID = port_stats.port_id GROUP BY sgpb.SECURITY_GROUP_ID ORDER BY pair_count_range DESC NULLS LAST) SELECT p.NETWORK_ID, MAX(inner_cte.pair_count_range) AS max_pair_count_range, MAX(inner_cte.pair_count_variance) AS max_pair_count_variance, MAX(inner_cte.pair_count_stddev) AS max_pair_count_stddev FROM inner_cte JOIN SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS AS sgpb ON inner_cte.SECURITY_GROUP_ID = sgpb.SECURITY_GROUP_ID JOIN PORTS AS p ON sgpb.PORT_ID = p.ID GROUP BY p.NETWORK_ID), CombinedNetworkMetrics AS (SELECT dsn.network_id, dsn.down_secure_ports, dsn.total_down_secure_ports_overall, aapsbn.max_pair_count_range, aapsbn.max_pair_count_variance, aapsbn.max_pair_count_stddev FROM DownSecureNetworks AS dsn JOIN AllowedAddressPairStatsByNetwork AS aapsbn ON dsn.network_id = aapsbn.network_id) SELECT * FROM CombinedNetworkMetrics ORDER BY network_id NULLS FIRST

question: For tenant ID '98333a1a28e746fa8c629c83a818ad57', for each qualifying administratively up port that is both bound to a security group and has at least one IP allocation, return the port ID, tenant ID, port name, MAC address, the number of security group bindings, the total number of DNS records on the port, the number of IP allocations, the total number of subnet-id rows from those allocations, along with the average number of IP allocations per qualifying port for that tenant. question: For DOWN ports in network ID `0a1d0a27-cffa-4de3-92c5-9d3fd3f2e74d`, return each port’s name, network ID, MAC address, admin state, status, device owner, bound security group ID, and the minimum admin_state_up over a window of 3 preceding and 1 following rows (ordered by port ID). question: For each network that contains an IPv4 subnet whose subnet ID is in ('012993ae-5d73-4aad-834b-e87a31e99d48'), show the network ID and the maximum dense-rank-to-max-standard-attribute ratio among those subnets in that network (where the ratio is computed as the dense rank of the subnet’s standard attribute ID ordered by the standard attribute updated-at timestamp using a window of the current row and 2 preceding rows, divided by the maximum subnet standard attribute ID considering the current row and the next 2 rows ordered by subnet ID).
evidence: Subnet ID "012993ae-5d73-4aad-834b-e87a31e99d48" is predicated by "subnets.id IN ('012993ae-5d73-4aad-834b-e87a31e99d48')"
generated_sql: WITH subnet_ratios AS (     SELECT         n.id AS network_id,         DENSE_RANK() OVER (             PARTITION BY n.id             ORDER BY sa.updated_at             ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW         )::numeric         / NULLIF(             MAX(s.standard_attr_id) OVER (                 PARTITION BY n.id                 ORDER BY s.id                 ROWS BETWEEN CURRENT ROW AND 2 FOLLOWING             )::numeric,             0         ) AS ratio     FROM networks AS n     JOIN subnets AS s         ON s.network_id = n.id     JOIN standardattributes AS sa         ON sa.id = s.standard_attr_id     WHERE s.ip_version = 4       AND s.id IN ('012993ae-5d73-4aad-834b-e87a31e99d48') ) SELECT network_id, MAX(ratio) AS max_ratio FROM subnet_ratios GROUP BY network_id
official_measure: BEAVER: the same set of rows
gold_sql: WITH inner_cte AS (WITH SubnetPools AS (SELECT s.NAME, s.TENANT_ID, s.NETWORK_ID, s.IP_VERSION, s.CIDR, s.GATEWAY_IP, s.ENABLE_DHCP, p.FIRST_IP, p.LAST_IP, MAX(s.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) OVER (ORDER BY s.ID NULLS FIRST ROWS BETWEEN CURRENT ROW AND 2 FOLLOWING) AS max_standard_attr_id_next2 FROM SUBNETS AS s JOIN IPALLOCATIONPOOLS AS p ON s.ID = p.SUBNET_ID WHERE s.IP_VERSION = 4 AND s.ID IN ('012993ae-5d73-4aad-834b-e87a31e99d48')), SubnetAttrDenseRank AS (SELECT s.NAME, DENSE_RANK() OVER (ORDER BY sa.UPDATED_AT NULLS FIRST ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) AS window_column FROM SUBNETS AS s JOIN STANDARDATTRIBUTES AS sa ON sa.ID = s.STANDARD_ATTR_ID WHERE s.IP_VERSION = 4 AND s.ID IN ('012993ae-5d73-4aad-834b-e87a31e99d48')) SELECT sp.NAME AS subnet_name, sp.TENANT_ID, sp.NETWORK_ID, sp.IP_VERSION, sp.CIDR, sp.GATEWAY_IP, sp.ENABLE_DHCP, sp.FIRST_IP AS allocation_pool_first_ip, sp.LAST_IP AS allocation_pool_last_ip, sp.max_standard_attr_id_next2, sadr.window_column AS standard_attr_dense_rank_window, ROUND(CAST(CAST(sadr.window_column AS DOUBLE PRECISION) / NULLIF(NULLIF(sp.max_standard_attr_id_next2, 0), 0) AS DECIMAL), 4) AS dense_rank_to_max_attr_ratio FROM SubnetPools AS sp JOIN SubnetAttrDenseRank AS sadr ON sp.NAME = sadr.NAME ORDER BY dense_rank_to_max_attr_ratio DESC NULLS LAST) SELECT network_id, MAX(dense_rank_to_max_attr_ratio) AS max_dense_rank_to_max_attr_ratio FROM inner_cte GROUP BY network_id

question: For tenant ID `17ea94ad74b64b9d92f4888336a598c7`, for each port that is administratively up and also has a binding on host `drive-59`, return the port ID, tenant ID, MAC address, the number of port security bindings on that port, the total number of times port security is enabled across those bindings, and the running sum of the port standard attribute IDs within each VIF type group (ordered by standard attribute ID). question: For ports whose status is DOWN, return each port’s ID and tenant ID along with its binding host and VIF type, allocated IP address (with a row number ordered by IP address using a window frame of 2 preceding rows and 1 following row), and also the port’s MAC address with the running sum of standard attribute IDs within each resource type group ordered by standard attribute ID. question: For each VIF type, show the VIF type, the number of DOWN ports, the average of the per-port windowed average admin_state_up (2 preceding and 2 following rows partitioned by VIF type and ordered by MAC address), and the average (across the involved hosts) variance of port standard attribute IDs for DOWN ports that have an IP allocation. generated_sql: WITH port_windowed AS (     SELECT         b.vif_type,         b.host,         p.id AS port_id,         p.status,         p.admin_state_up,         p.standard_attr_id,         AVG(p.admin_state_up) OVER (             PARTITION BY b.vif_type             ORDER BY p.mac_address             ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND 2 FOLLOWING         ) AS windowed_avg_admin_state_up     FROM ml2_port_bindings AS b     JOIN ports AS p       ON p.id = b.port_id ), vif_type_metrics AS (     SELECT         vif_type,         COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE status = 'DOWN') AS down_port_count,         AVG(windowed_avg_admin_state_up) AS avg_windowed_admin_state_up     FROM port_windowed     GROUP BY vif_type ), host_variances AS (     SELECT DISTINCT         pw.vif_type,         pw.host,         VARIANCE(pw.standard_attr_id) OVER (             PARTITION BY pw.vif_type, pw.host         ) AS standard_attr_id_variance     FROM port_windowed AS pw     WHERE pw.status = 'DOWN'       AND EXISTS (           SELECT 1           FROM ipallocations AS ia           WHERE ia.port_id = pw.port_id       ) ), vif_type_host_variances AS (     SELECT         vif_type,         AVG(standard_attr_id_variance) AS avg_host_variance     FROM host_variances     GROUP BY vif_type ) SELECT     m.vif_type,     m.down_port_count,     m.avg_windowed_admin_state_up,     v.avg_host_variance FROM vif_type_metrics AS m LEFT JOIN vif_type_host_variances AS v   ON m.vif_type IS NOT DISTINCT FROM v.vif_type
official_measure: BEAVER: the same set of rows
gold_sql: WITH DownPortsWindow AS (SELECT p.NAME, p.MAC_ADDRESS, p.ADMIN_STATE_UP, b.HOST, b.VIF_TYPE, AVG(p.ADMIN_STATE_UP) OVER (PARTITION BY b.VIF_TYPE ORDER BY p.MAC_ADDRESS NULLS FIRST ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND 2 FOLLOWING) AS window_column FROM PORTS AS p JOIN ML2_PORT_BINDINGS AS b ON p.ID = b.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' ORDER BY p.MAC_ADDRESS NULLS FIRST), HostStandardAttrVariance AS (SELECT b.HOST, VAR_POP(p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) AS standard_attr_id_variance FROM ML2_PORT_BINDINGS AS b JOIN PORTS AS p ON b.PORT_ID = p.ID JOIN IPALLOCATIONS AS ia ON p.ID = ia.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' AND NOT ia.PORT_ID IS NULL GROUP BY b.HOST ORDER BY standard_attr_id_variance DESC NULLS LAST) SELECT dpw.VIF_TYPE, COUNT(*) AS down_ports_count, AVG(dpw.window_column) AS avg_window_admin_state_up, AVG(hsav.standard_attr_id_variance) AS avg_standard_attr_id_variance_across_hosts FROM DownPortsWindow AS dpw JOIN HostStandardAttrVariance AS hsav ON dpw.HOST = hsav.HOST GROUP BY dpw.VIF_TYPE ORDER BY down_ports_count DESC NULLS LAST

question: Find load balancers associated with the provider named 'haproxy' whose highest admin_state_up value is 1, and for each such load balancer return its name and operating status along with the total incoming bytes for that operating status across ACTIVE-provisioning load balancers, keeping only operating statuses where the total incoming bytes exceed 1,000,000. generated_sql: WITH haproxy_lbs AS (     SELECT lb.id, lb.name, lb.operating_status, lb.admin_state_up     FROM lbaas_loadbalancers AS lb     WHERE EXISTS (         SELECT 1         FROM flavors AS f         JOIN flavorserviceprofilebindings AS fsb           ON fsb.flavor_id = f.id         JOIN serviceprofiles AS sp           ON sp.id = fsb.service_profile_id         WHERE f.id = lb.flavor_id           AND sp.driver = 'haproxy'     ) ), max_admin_state AS (     SELECT MAX(admin_state_up) AS max_admin_state_up     FROM haproxy_lbs ), active_status_bytes AS (     SELECT lb.operating_status,            SUM(COALESCE(stats.bytes_in, 0)) AS total_incoming_bytes     FROM lbaas_loadbalancers AS lb     LEFT JOIN lbaas_loadbalancer_statistics AS stats       ON stats.loadbalancer_id = lb.id     WHERE lb.provisioning_status = 'ACTIVE'     GROUP BY lb.operating_status     HAVING SUM(COALESCE(stats.bytes_in, 0)) > 1000000 ) SELECT h.name,        h.operating_status,        b.total_incoming_bytes FROM haproxy_lbs AS h JOIN max_admin_state AS m   ON h.admin_state_up = m.max_admin_state_up JOIN active_status_bytes AS b   ON b.operating_status = h.operating_status WHERE m.max_admin_state_up = 1
official_measure: BEAVER: the same set of rows
gold_sql: WITH ActiveStatusBytes AS (SELECT lb.OPERATING_STATUS, SUM(s.BYTES_IN) AS total_bytes_in FROM LBAAS_LOADBALANCERS AS lb JOIN LBAAS_LOADBALANCER_STATISTICS AS s ON lb.ID = s.LOADBALANCER_ID WHERE lb.PROVISIONING_STATUS = 'ACTIVE' GROUP BY lb.OPERATING_STATUS HAVING SUM(s.BYTES_IN) > 1000000), HaproxyAdminUpLoadBalancers AS (SELECT lb.name AS loadbalancer_name, MAX(lb.admin_state_up) AS max_admin_state_up, lb.operating_status FROM LBAAS_LOADBALANCERS AS lb JOIN PROVIDERRESOURCEASSOCIATIONS AS pra ON lb.id = pra.resource_id WHERE pra.provider_name = 'haproxy' GROUP BY lb.name, lb.operating_status HAVING MAX(lb.admin_state_up) = 1) SELECT h.loadbalancer_name, h.operating_status, a.total_bytes_in FROM HaproxyAdminUpLoadBalancers AS h JOIN ActiveStatusBytes AS a ON h.operating_status = a.OPERATING_STATUS ORDER BY h.operating_status NULLS FIRST, h.loadbalancer_name NULLS FIRST

question: For each network status, show the variance and standard deviation (using STDDEV only and never STDDEV_POP) of PORT_SECURITY_ENABLED across networks with at least one security binding, along with the total number of ports (restricted to standard attributes where RESOURCE_TYPE = 'ports') for that same status; also list, for the matching port status, each device owner’s port count and the earliest standard attribute UPDATED_AT timestamp. generated_sql: WITH network_security_stats AS (     SELECT         n.status AS network_status,         VARIANCE(nsb.port_security_enabled) AS port_security_variance,         STDDEV(nsb.port_security_enabled) AS port_security_stddev     FROM networks AS n     JOIN networksecuritybindings AS nsb         ON nsb.network_id = n.id     GROUP BY n.status ), matching_ports AS (     SELECT         n.status AS network_status,         p.status AS port_status,         p.device_owner,         sa.updated_at     FROM networks AS n     JOIN ports AS p         ON p.network_id = n.id        AND p.status = n.status     JOIN standardattributes AS sa         ON sa.id = p.standard_attr_id     WHERE sa.resource_type = 'ports' ), port_totals AS (     SELECT         network_status,         COUNT(*) AS total_port_count     FROM matching_ports     GROUP BY network_status ), port_owner_stats AS (     SELECT DISTINCT         network_status,         port_status,         device_owner,         COUNT(*) OVER (             PARTITION BY network_status, device_owner         ) AS owner_port_count,         MIN(updated_at) OVER (             PARTITION BY network_status, device_owner         ) AS earliest_updated_at     FROM matching_ports ) SELECT     nss.network_status,     nss.port_security_variance,     nss.port_security_stddev,     COALESCE(pt.total_port_count, 0) AS total_port_count,     pos.port_status,     pos.device_owner,     pos.owner_port_count,     pos.earliest_updated_at FROM network_security_stats AS nss LEFT JOIN port_totals AS pt     ON pt.network_status = nss.network_status LEFT JOIN port_owner_stats AS pos     ON pos.network_status = nss.network_status ORDER BY nss.network_status, pos.device_owner
official_measure: BEAVER: the same set of rows
gold_sql: WITH NetworkSecurityStats AS (SELECT n.STATUS AS network_status, VAR_POP(nsb.PORT_SECURITY_ENABLED) AS port_security_enabled_variance, STDDEV_POP(nsb.PORT_SECURITY_ENABLED) AS port_security_enabled_stddev FROM NETWORKS AS n JOIN NETWORKSECURITYBINDINGS AS nsb ON n.ID = nsb.NETWORK_ID GROUP BY n.STATUS ORDER BY port_security_enabled_variance DESC NULLS LAST), PortOwnerStats AS (SELECT p.STATUS AS port_status, p.DEVICE_OWNER AS device_owner, COUNT(p.ID) AS port_count, MIN(sa.UPDATED_AT) AS earliest_standard_attr_update FROM PORTS AS p JOIN STANDARDATTRIBUTES AS sa ON sa.ID = p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID WHERE sa.RESOURCE_TYPE = 'ports' GROUP BY p.STATUS, p.DEVICE_OWNER), NetworkPortCountsByStatus AS (SELECT n.STATUS AS network_status, COUNT(p.ID) AS total_ports_in_status FROM NETWORKS AS n JOIN PORTS AS p ON p.NETWORK_ID = n.ID JOIN STANDARDATTRIBUTES AS sa ON sa.ID = p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID WHERE sa.RESOURCE_TYPE = 'ports' GROUP BY n.STATUS) SELECT nss.network_status, nss.port_security_enabled_variance, nss.port_security_enabled_stddev, npc.total_ports_in_status, pos.port_status, pos.device_owner, pos.port_count, pos.earliest_standard_attr_update FROM NetworkSecurityStats AS nss JOIN NetworkPortCountsByStatus AS npc ON nss.network_status = npc.network_status JOIN PortOwnerStats AS pos ON pos.port_status = nss.network_status ORDER BY npc.total_ports_in_status DESC NULLS LAST, nss.port_security_enabled_variance DESC NULLS LAST, pos.port_count DESC NULLS LAST

question: For each port that is DOWN and also has admin_state_up = 1 with at least one security group binding, list the port ID, tenant ID, port name, network ID, MAC address, device owner, allocated IP address, the row number within its network (ordered by port ID), the number of security group bindings, the total number of DNS records, and the DNS-records-per-security-group-binding ratio rounded to 2 decimals.
generated_sql: WITH security_group_counts AS (     SELECT port_id, COUNT(*) AS binding_count     FROM securitygroupportbindings     GROUP BY port_id ), dns_counts AS (     SELECT port_id, COUNT(*) AS dns_record_count     FROM portdnses     GROUP BY port_id ), ip_addresses AS (     SELECT         port_id,         ARRAY_AGG(DISTINCT ip_address ORDER BY ip_address)             FILTER (WHERE ip_address IS NOT NULL) AS allocated_ip_addresses     FROM ipallocations     GROUP BY port_id ), eligible_ports AS (     SELECT         p.id AS port_id,         p.tenant_id,         p.name,         p.network_id,         p.mac_address,         p.device_owner,         ROW_NUMBER() OVER (             PARTITION BY p.network_id             ORDER BY p.id         ) AS network_row_number,         sg.binding_count,         COALESCE(dns.dns_record_count, 0) AS dns_record_count     FROM ports AS p     JOIN security_group_counts AS sg         ON sg.port_id = p.id     LEFT JOIN dns_counts AS dns         ON dns.port_id = p.id     WHERE p.status = 'DOWN'       AND p.admin_state_up = 1 ) SELECT     ep.port_id,     ep.tenant_id,     ep.name,     ep.network_id,     ep.mac_address,     ep.device_owner,     COALESCE(ips.allocated_ip_addresses, ARRAY[]::TEXT[]) AS allocated_ip_addresses,     ep.network_row_number,     ep.binding_count AS security_group_binding_count,     ep.dns_record_count,     ROUND(ep.dns_record_count::NUMERIC / ep.binding_count, 2)         AS dns_records_per_security_group_binding FROM eligible_ports AS ep LEFT JOIN ip_addresses AS ips     ON ips.port_id = ep.port_id ORDER BY ep.network_id, ep.port_id
official_measure: BEAVER: the same set of rows
gold_sql: WITH PortSecurityAndDNS AS (SELECT p.id AS port_id, p.tenant_id, p.name AS port_name, COUNT(sgpb.security_group_id) AS security_group_binding_count, SUM(CASE WHEN pd.port_id IS NULL THEN 0 ELSE 1 END) AS dns_record_count FROM SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS AS sgpb JOIN PORTS AS p ON sgpb.port_id = p.id LEFT JOIN PORTDNSES AS pd ON p.id = pd.port_id WHERE p.admin_state_up = 1 GROUP BY p.id, p.tenant_id, p.name), DownPortsWithIPs AS (SELECT p.ID AS port_id, p.TENANT_ID AS tenant_id, p.NAME AS port_name, p.NETWORK_ID AS network_id, p.MAC_ADDRESS AS mac_address, p.DEVICE_OWNER AS device_owner, ia.IP_ADDRESS AS ip_address, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY p.NETWORK_ID ORDER BY p.ID NULLS FIRST) AS window_column FROM PORTS AS p JOIN IPALLOCATIONS AS ia ON p.ID = ia.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN') SELECT d.port_id, d.tenant_id, d.port_name, d.network_id, d.mac_address, d.device_owner, d.ip_address, d.window_column, psd.security_group_binding_count, psd.dns_record_count, ROUND(CAST(CAST(psd.dns_record_count AS DOUBLE PRECISION) / NULLIF(NULLIF(psd.security_group_binding_count, 0), 0) AS DECIMAL), 2) AS dns_records_per_security_group_binding FROM DownPortsWithIPs AS d JOIN PortSecurityAndDNS AS psd ON psd.port_id = d.port_id ORDER BY dns_records_per_security_group_binding DESC NULLS LAST, d.network_id NULLS FIRST, d.window_column NULLS FIRST

question: For active networks, list (per tenant) the first network by name (row_number = 1) along with the subnet (by subnet name) on that network that has at least one DNS nameserver entry, and show the subnet’s IP allocation pool count range, variance, and standard deviation (using STDDEV only and never STDDEV_POP) together with the network’s admin_state_up flag, MTU, and standard-attribute updated_at timestamp. Do not return any rounded answers.
generated_sql: WITH ranked_networks AS (     SELECT         n.tenant_id,         n.id AS network_id,         n.name AS network_name,         n.admin_state_up,         n.mtu,         sa.updated_at,         ROW_NUMBER() OVER (             PARTITION BY n.tenant_id             ORDER BY n.name, n.id         ) AS rn     FROM networks AS n     JOIN standardattributes AS sa         ON n.standard_attr_id = sa.id     WHERE n.status = 'ACTIVE' ), allocation_pool_stats AS (     SELECT         subnet_id,         COUNT(*) AS pool_count,         MIN(first_ip::inet) AS range_start,         MAX(last_ip::inet) AS range_end,         VARIANCE((last_ip::inet - first_ip::inet + 1)::numeric) AS pool_size_variance,         STDDEV((last_ip::inet - first_ip::inet + 1)::numeric) AS pool_size_stddev     FROM ipallocationpools     GROUP BY subnet_id ) SELECT     rn.tenant_id,     rn.network_name,     s.name AS subnet_name,     COALESCE(aps.pool_count, 0) AS pool_count,     aps.range_start,     aps.range_end,     aps.pool_size_variance,     aps.pool_size_stddev,     rn.admin_state_up,     rn.mtu,     rn.updated_at FROM ranked_networks AS rn JOIN subnets AS s     ON s.network_id = rn.network_id LEFT JOIN allocation_pool_stats AS aps     ON aps.subnet_id = s.id WHERE rn.rn = 1   AND EXISTS (       SELECT 1       FROM dnsnameservers AS d       WHERE d.subnet_id = s.id   ) ORDER BY rn.tenant_id, s.name
official_measure: BEAVER: the same set of rows
gold_sql: WITH SubnetPoolStats AS (SELECT s.name AS subnet_name, MAX(pool_count) - MIN(pool_count) AS pool_count_range, VAR_POP(pool_count) AS pool_count_variance, STDDEV_POP(pool_count) AS pool_count_stddev FROM subnets AS s JOIN dnsnameservers AS d ON d.subnet_id = s.id JOIN (SELECT s2.id AS subnet_id, COUNT(*) AS pool_count FROM subnets AS s2 JOIN ipallocationpools AS p ON p.subnet_id = s2.id GROUP BY s2.id, p.id) AS pool_stats ON pool_stats.subnet_id = s.id GROUP BY s.name ORDER BY pool_count_range DESC NULLS LAST), ActiveNetworks AS (SELECT n.ID AS network_id, n.NAME AS network_name, n.TENANT_ID AS tenant_id, n.ADMIN_STATE_UP AS admin_state_up, n.MTU AS mtu, sa.UPDATED_AT AS standard_attr_updated_at, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY n.TENANT_ID ORDER BY n.NAME NULLS FIRST) AS window_column FROM NETWORKS AS n JOIN STANDARDATTRIBUTES AS sa ON sa.ID = n.STANDARD_ATTR_ID WHERE n.STATUS = 'ACTIVE') SELECT an.tenant_id, an.network_id, an.network_name, an.admin_state_up, an.mtu, an.standard_attr_updated_at, an.window_column, sps.subnet_name, sps.pool_count_range, sps.pool_count_variance, sps.pool_count_stddev FROM ActiveNetworks AS an JOIN subnets AS s ON s.network_id = an.network_id JOIN SubnetPoolStats AS sps ON sps.subnet_name = s.name WHERE an.window_column = 1 ORDER BY sps.pool_count_range DESC NULLS LAST, an.tenant_id NULLS FIRST, an.network_name NULLS FIRST

question: From the top 10 networks with the most DOWN ports, list each network ID and its DOWN-port count, and for each DOWN port show the port ID, tenant ID, port name, MAC address, device owner, allocated IP address, binding host, VIF type, the port’s row number within its network (ordered by port ID), and the port’s rank within the DOWN status group (ordered by port ID).
